passages.heading: Overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body:
i. Provides expert space analysis to support Army and Joint, Interagency, Intergovernmental, and Multinational (JIIM) partner plans and operations. ii. Coordinates with staff to integrate space capabilities supporting Information and Influence Activities (IIA), Information Operations (IO), Electronic Warfare (EW), Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, and Targeting Operations (IJSTO), and cyber activities. iii. Demonstrates proficiency in space integration and interdiction operations, including Space Control Electronic Warfare (SCEW), Offensive operations (Counter-SATCOM and NAVWAR), and Defensive operations (SATCOM Monitoring and Assured Positioning, Navigation & Timing). iv. Possesses expertise in space systems and unified land operations, enabling effective performance in high-level positions (Army and JIIM partners) with minimal guidance and close interaction with senior decision-makers.
v. Conducts force and crisis intervention planning and operations related to space. vi. Understands space procedures and infrastructure for tasking, processing, and utilizing space products, as well as telemetry, tracking, and commanding of space systems. vii. Translates complex space concepts and systems into clear terms for warfighters and systems developers. viii. Leverages current and future space-based technologies in innovative ways to address emerging military challenges. ix. Utilizes modeling, simulation, analysis, and other tools to develop and employ space capabilities.
x. Contributes to the development and integration of policy, concepts, requirements, and acquisition for space capabilities. xi. Communicates technical information and concepts clearly and accurately, providing presentations, education, and training within organizations as required. xii. Delivers timely alerts of Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) launches by utilizing a network of space-based and ground-based sensors. xiii. Tracks incoming missile threats and accurately distinguishes warheads from decoys or debris, ensuring precise targeting. xiv. Enables real-time situational awareness, threat assessment, and coordinated engagement decisions. xv. Enables the launch of Ground-Based Interceptors (GBIs) and supplies in-flight guidance to ensure successful interception of threats during the midcourse phase. xvi. Evaluates the outcome of engagements, confirming whether the threat has been neutralized through sensor feedback and post-intercept analysis. xvii. Maintains operational readiness by continuously monitoring, testing, and maintaining all components to ensure rapid response capability. xviii. Facilitates data sharing and operational coordination with other U.S. and allied missile defense systems, supporting a layered defense architecture.
8. Special Qualifications. All Space Operations Specialists must maintain a Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance.
9. Military Occupational Specialty 40D, The Professional Development Model. The model focuses on the quality and range of experience rather than specific gates or assignments required for progression.
i. Assignments. Assignments facilitate the accumulation of experience over time, providing opportunities to employ and further develop the skills and knowledge acquired through institutional training. Every assignment is invaluable to an NCO’s professional development and necessary for the success of our mission. HRC assigns IAW talent management guidelines that dictate how NCOs’ qualifications are matched to unit requirements. Talent is the intersection of three dimensions, KSBs. A Service Member’s talent will be determined using displayed performance/potential (NCOERs, DA 1059s, Institutional Training acquired, etc.). Individuals with the most outstanding talent merit the assignments with the greatest responsibility. When possible, an NCO should always prioritize completion of their respective Critical Leader Developmental (CLD) assignments. After completion of CLD assignments, NCOs should seek broadening assignments that demonstrate their initiative, versatility, and potential for increased responsibility. NCOs must bear in mind that, regardless of the given assignment, performance evaluations will carry more weight than an assigned duty title. ii. Assignments expand a leader’s capabilities by exposing them to different organizational cultures and environments. Assignments are grouped into four bins: a) Institutional and Functional Assignments. MTOE unit; task force; Army Service Component Command and below assignments; ASCC/Corps/Divisions/Special Forces Groups; Space Support Elements; TDA unit; USASMDC, HQDA G-3/5/7. b) Joint and Multinational Assignments. Joint Staff, USEUCOM, USAFRICOM, USSOCOM, USSTRATCOM, USCYBERCOM, USSPACECOM, USINDOPACOM, USNORTHCOM, USSOUTHCOM, Joint Navigation Warfare Center (JNWC), Theater Special Operations Commands (TSOCs), NORAD, and NATO. c) Inter-Agency and Inter-Governmental Assignments. OSD, NRO, DISA, DIA. d) Civilian Enterprise and Academia Assignments. TWI, instructor positions at NPS, USMA, AWC, CAC, and Army Scholarship/Fellowship/Internship program. iii. Key (nominative) billets. A CMF may further optimize the distribution of NCO talent by selecting the best-qualified NCOs based on their KSBs to key positions across the enterprise. The CMF 40 Proponent designates these positions for experienced leaders of character who demonstrate potential and have proven their competence in a broad range of environments. Positive performance in key billets should signal superior performance and potential. Nominative assignments are specialized broadening positions typically reserved for highly skilled and experienced personnel. Individuals who are hand-selected by the Regimental CSM or position SGM for these assignments have demonstrated exceptional leadership qualities, expertise in their field, and a proven track record of success. HRC considers these billets as critical leader development assignments. iv. Critical leader developmental assignments (CLD). Critical leader development positions are deemed fundamental to an NCO’s development within their CMF. These positions entail direct leadership over Soldiers and NCOs within your MOS/CMF. Operational or generating MOS and CMF positions are identified by a respective proponent and revised periodically to develop critical technical and leadership skills and experience that advance the capabilities of the CMF and Army profession. Positive performance in these positions provides the greatest potential for advancement.
v. Operational assignments. Primarily a modified table of organization and equipment assignment with duties in your MOS or CMF at the battalion level or higher. These assignments provide the NCO with an opportunity to gain knowledge and experience at the organizational level. Command Staff positions are valued because they develop the NCO’s understanding and capabilities at the strategic echelon, instilling the desired KSBs required for future billets of additional rank and responsibility. vi. Key Development Definition. Key Developmental (KD) applies to Active Component Noncommissioned Officers or a specific duty position at their current grade in a specific time, IAW the CMF 40 Career model. KD positions are essential in the growth and development of the military leadership and MOS core competencies. ACROSS CMF 40, SSGs, SFC, MSG/1SG KD MUST BE A MINIMUM OF 18 MONTHS, 36 MONTHS PREFERRED. If SM is serving in a position of higher grade with appropriate enumerations/ratings on their NCOER, that time will count towards their current rank KD time requirements.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The quality and success of a Soldier’s career are in direct proportion to the Soldier’s consistent commitment to excellence, regardless of the mission. Soldiers should strive to improve in the Institutional, Operational, and Self-Development domains. The Soldiers committed to achieving high goals will develop leadership skills and have the practical knowledge and ambition to put them to good use.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Soldiers at this level and above should study and master the following military publications: ADP 1-0, ADP 6-22, ADP 7-0, ADRP 1, FM 7-22, TC 7-21.13, AR 600-20, AR 670-1, DA Pam 670-1, STP 21-1-SMCT, FM 3-14, ATP 3-14.1 (Army Space Control Operations), ATP 3-14.3 (Techniques for Army Space Forces), and FM 3-27 (Global MD), all -10 level technical manuals associated with their equipment, Individual Critical Task Lists (ICTL), and all crew drills related to their respective equipment and current assignment found through the Central Army Registry.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Familiarization and use of online resources such as Army Training Network (ATN), Integrated Personnel and Pay System-Army (IPPS-A), Center for Army Lessons Learned (CALL), S1Net (SharePoint), Army Space Knowledge Management Site (ASKMS) at https://armyeitaas.sharepoint-mil.us/sites/ASKMS, and U.S. Army Human Resources Command (HRC) are essential for staying up to date on the latest Army and Space Operations Branch information.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Soldier boards such as Best Warrior Competition, Soldier of the Month, Quarter, and/or Year to help broaden the knowledge base, instill discipline, and improve the Soldier’s ability to communicate verbally. Soldiers should also strive to earn the Expert Soldier Badge (ESB) by demonstrating their tactical proficiency.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Pursuing advanced education is a critical aspect of a self-development program. The pace of operational assignments may limit the opportunity for civilian education; however, Soldiers who are willing to make the required sacrifices should seize all available opportunities. The College-Level Examination Program (CLEP) and the Defense Activity for Non-Traditional Education Support (DANTES) are available to Soldiers who are unable to pursue formal civilian courses. A Soldier’s own desire to excel drives the enrollment and completion of these self-development options. Ample opportunities exist for Soldiers to participate in various correspondence and distance learning courses to accomplish individual educational objectives.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Soldiers may also earn promotion points for Technical Certification; find the list of Certifications on the COOL website at http://www.cool.osd.mil. For information on these and other education programs, visit the Army Education Center (AEC) on your installation. Every Soldier should explore and complete appropriate credentials for their military occupational specialties and/or additional training they have been provided, as it demonstrates to leaders and the Army that they have mastered those skills.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Operational assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: 40D1O Soldiers should focus on building a strong foundation of technical expertise in equipment, research and data collection, mastering basic MOS skills, and developing proficiency in common Warrior and Soldier tasks. They should seek opportunities to demonstrate initiative, leadership, and team-leading abilities while gaining crucial experience as space operators. The 40D should emphasize the successful performance in their roles, the development of technical skills, the honing of tactical proficiency, and the building of a solid foundation of tactical knowledge. Soldiers should strive to serve in positions of increased responsibility whenever possible.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Education
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Army Space Cadre Basic Course (ASCBC), Army Space Control Fundamentals (ASCF), Army GMD Staff Course (AGSC), Tactical Space Operations Course (TSOC).

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Key Developmental Assignments (KDAs)
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: None.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Developmental/Broadening
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: NA.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Self-Development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Begin pursuing an associate degree or higher-level civilian education opportunities. Complete the prerequisites for attendance at BLC. Airborne, Air Assault, Basic Combatives Course (Level I), Digital Training Management System (DTMS) Course, Unit Armorer Course, Drivers Training, and the Expert Soldier Badge.

passages.heading: vii. Space Operations Specialist (SPC/CPL) Development — Core Competencies
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Tactical and technical proficiency, Leadership, Space Operations Fundamentals.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Space Sergeants are dutiful leaders who serve as team leaders and operators of space equipment and systems. They supervise Skill level one entry-level Soldiers, so they should focus on team development and leadership skills to train and motivate subordinate operators in a dynamic, technical field. They must build entry-level project management and delegation skills as they lead teams to properly operate and maintain space and missile defense equipment or systems. Sergeants must develop sound communication and management skills as they learn to lead space operations teams across the full spectrum of joint combat operations. The quality and success of a Sergeant’s career is in direct proportion to a consistent commitment to excellence, regardless of the mission. Sergeants committed to achieving high goals will develop leadership skills and have the practical knowledge and ambition to put them to good use. The Sergeant’s career progression relies upon a strong drive to excel in duty performance and space operations proficiency in addition to the attainment of additional knowledge, skills, and behaviors (KSBs) related to leadership and MOS competency.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Sergeants should focus on mastering the military publications listed at the preceding skill level, expand proficiency across the array of Army doctrinal, operational, and technical publications, and become familiar with where to find them. Sergeants should study and master the following additional military publications: ADP 3-0; ADP 6-22; FM 6–22; AR 25-50; ADP 7-0; FM 7-22; STP-21-24-SMCT. While continuing to build their proficiency in FM 3-14, ATP 3-14.1 (Army Space Control Operations), ATP 3-14.3 (Techniques for Army Space Forces), and FM 3-27 (Global MD), Individual Critical Task Lists (ICTL), and all crew drills associated with their respective equipment and current assignment found through the Central Army Registry.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Familiarization and use of online resources and social media sites such as CALL, ATN, IPPS-A, S1Net (SharePoint), ASKMS, and HRC are essential for staying up to date on the latest Army and Space operations information.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Participate in competitive boards such as Best Warrior Competition, NCO of the Month, Quarter, and/or Year, the SGT Audie Murphy/SGT Morales Clubs to broaden the knowledge base, instill discipline, and improve the NCO’s ability to communicate verbally. NCOs should also strive to earn the Expert Soldier Badge (ESB), demonstrating their tactical proficiency.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Obtaining recognition as the Honor Graduate, Distinguished Honor Graduate, or Commandant’s List at all PME schools or any course attended should be the goal of all SGTs.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Suggested for self-development at this level are the Enlisted Joint Professional Military Education (EJPME) Course, DAU Courses, and Skillport Classes. Additional reading materials can be found in the Army Training Information System (ATIS) at https://learn.atis.army.mil/moodle/.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Sergeants may also earn promotion points for Technical Certification; a list of certifications is available on the COOL website at http://www.cool.osd.mil. For information on these and other education programs, visit the Army Education Center (AEC) on your installation. Every Sergeant should explore and complete appropriate credentials for their military occupational specialties and/or additional training they have been provided, as it demonstrates to leaders and the Army that they have mastered those skills.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Reclassification
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: If an NCO at this grade reclassifies into Space Operations, they must complete CLD assignments within their new MOS before being considered for assignments in broadening opportunities.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Operational assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The focus during this phase of a career should be tactical assignments, developing the Soldier’s leadership skills, honing technical expertise, and laying a foundation of tactical knowledge. At every opportunity, NCOs should seek positions that provide them with leadership experience. The Key Leadership Position for a Sergeant is Team Leader or Crew Chief. Boards and leaders may view a Sergeant with 18 months of key leadership time as qualified, 24 months as highly qualified, and 30 months or more as most qualified. Drill Sergeant may fulfill the NCO’s requirement for a key leadership position if the NCO has not had an opportunity to serve in the capacity of Team Leader or Crew Chief in the operating force.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Education
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: No PME Requirement.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Key Developmental Assignments (KDAs)
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Team Leader.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Developmental/Broadening
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Drill Sergeant and Recruiter.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Self-Development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Air Assault School, Basic Airborne Course, CBRN NCO, Field Sanitation Team Training, Hazardous Materials (OSHA), Security Manager Course, Tactical Combatives Course Level II, TC-AIMS II Unit Movement I & II, TC-AIMS, Unit Prevention Leader (UPL), and Unit Rail/Air Loading Training Course. Pursue an associate degree or higher-level civilian education. Study Army publications directly related to MOS proficiency and core competencies. Participate in NCO of the Month/Quarter/Year Boards.

passages.heading: viii. Space Operations Sergeant (SGT) Development — Core Competencies
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Tactical and technical proficiency, Leadership, Space Operations Fundamentals.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The quality and success of a Staff Sergeant’s career are in direct proportion to a consistent commitment to excellence, regardless of the mission. Staff Sergeants who are committed to achieving high goals will develop leadership skills and have the practical knowledge and ambition to put them to good use. This is typically the first level of leadership at which the NCO is responsible for leading other leaders. Staff Sergeants should continue to hone their leadership skills and maintain a high level of proficiency in their space operations tasks. The Staff Sergeant’s career progression relies upon a strong drive to excel in duty performance and space operations proficiency, in addition to the attainment of additional KSBs related to leadership and MOS competency.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: In addition to military publications listed previously, SSGs should study and become familiar with military publications related to equipment and duty skills associated with their current MOS and assignment such as: STP 21- 24, ADP 6-22, FM 7-0, ADP 7- 0, SSGs should begin to develop familiarization with all ADPs, ADRPs, and the Unit Combined Arms Training Strategies (CATS). These provide standard unit training strategies to support Department of the Army (DA) unit operational tempo and resource projections, and to assist unit commanders in developing unit training plans that integrate standards in weapons training and the core mission essential task list (CMETL). Access military publications through the Army Publishing Directorate (APD) at https://www.armypubs.army.mil/.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The Army urges SSGs to seek opportunities to pursue completion of an associate degree, credentialing, professional certifications, and apprenticeship opportunities.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: NCO boards such as Best Warrior Competition, NCO of the Month, Quarter, and/or Year, and the SGT Audie Murphy/SGT Morales Clubs to broaden the knowledge base, instill discipline, improve communication skills and leadership potential, build more adaptive leaders, and set the example for Soldiers to follow. Staff Sergeants should host mock boards and volunteer for competitive board membership.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Suggested for self-development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: the following for self-development: TC 7-22.7 (The Noncommissioned Officer Guide) and all publications referenced in Appendix B; ADP 6-22; ADP 3-0; DA Pam 600-25; FM 7- 22; and ADP 1.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The best-qualified SSGs should have 24 months of rated time in an authorized leadership position. Possess one or more of the following qualifications: a consistently strong pattern of far exceeded standard ratings on their DA Forms 2166-9-2 with a consistent pattern of senior rater comments that clearly state strong potential to serve at the next higher grade, completion of 60 semester hours toward an associate degree, or recognition as a Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate or top 20% Commandant’s list during NCOES or MOS enhancing courses.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Staff Sergeants should seek generating force and broadening assignments such as Drill Sergeant, Recruiter, ALC Small Group Leader, Instructor, and Training with Industry (TWI), which will aid in distinguishing them from their peers.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Reclassification
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: If an NCO at this grade reclassifies into Space Operations, they must complete CLD assignments within their new MOS before being considered for assignments in broadening opportunities.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Operational assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Seek assignments in the Operating Force at company and BN levels focused on continued development and refinement of leadership skills, staff products and MOS competency. Seek tough leadership positions and excel in the performance of the duties associated with those positions. Boards and Leaders may view SSGs who complete 18 months of key leadership time as qualified, 24 months of key leadership time as highly qualified, and 36 months or more as most qualified to build the requisite KSBs to be successful in the next grade.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Education
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Basic Leader Course (BLC) and Advanced Leader Course (ALC)

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Key Developmental Assignments (KDAs)
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Drill Sergeant and Recruiter.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Developmental/Broadening
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Instructor, Enlisted Aide, BLC Small Group Leader, Training with Industry, Observer Controller/Trainer, ALC Small Group Leader.

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Self-Development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Airborne, Jumpmaster, Air Assault, Ranger, Master Fitness Trainer, Battle Staff, Master Driver Trainer, Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention (SHARP), Equal Opportunity Leader, HAZMAT Course, and Enlisted Aide Training Course. Pursue higher-level civilian education opportunities. Stand before the Sergeant Audie Murphy Board, Sergeant Morales Board, and/or NCO of the Month/Quarter/Year Board. Earn the Army Recruiter Gold Badge, Army Master Recruiter Badge, Basic Army Instructor Badge, Senior Army Instructor Badge, and/or the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal (MOVSM).

passages.heading: ix. Senior Space Operations Sergeant (SSG) Development — Core Competencies
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Tactical and technical proficiency, Leadership, Space Operations Fundamentals.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: As NCOs become more senior, self-motivated development becomes increasingly important. Leaders will evaluate the Sergeant First Class less on their individual accomplishments and more on building a productive space operations organization capable of achieving mission success. Activities such as professional reading or college courses help Senior NCOs develop the organizational leadership skills needed to coach, teach, and mentor Soldiers. This is typically the first level of leadership at which the NCO is responsible for developing organizations (platoons/sections). The Sergeant First Class’s career progression relies upon a strong drive to excel in duty performance and space operations proficiency, in addition to the attainment of additional KSBs related to leadership and MOS competency.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: These NCOs should study and master the following additional military publications: AR 350–1, AR 750–1, all -10 level maintenance manuals related to their equipment, and battle drills associated with their current assignment. The Army suggests the following for self-development: The NCO professional reading list in TC 7–22.7, ADP 6-22, NCOPDS (NCO 2020), and the NCO guide all contain additional reading material for self- development.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — The self-development process should now shift to advanced skills
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Ideally, if a Soldier used tuition assistance to the maximum extent, a Sergeant First Class could have completed an associate’s degree or an equivalent number of semester hours at this point in their career and continue studies toward an undergraduate degree. Sergeants First Class must continue to remain competent in technical fields and tactical skills while focusing on broadening their leadership, management, and doctrinal knowledge. Subjects such as organizational behavior, personnel management, time management, Army operations at the operational and strategic levels, and battle staff functions should be the focus of self-development.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Soldiers should also consider entering a program to gain nationally recognized credentials in an appropriate technical discipline. Soldiers may also earn technical certifications; a list of certifications can be found on the COOL website. For information on these and other education programs, visit the AEC on your installation.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: NCO Boards such as Best Warrior Competition, NCO of the Month, Quarter, and/or Year, and the SGT Audie Murphy/SGT Morales Clubs to broaden the knowledge base, instill discipline, and improve the SFC’s ability to communicate.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Broaden their focus to include functional training such as Battle Staff, Master Fitness Trainer (MFT), Equal Opportunity (EO), and Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention (SHARP) representative to add value to the organization.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Sergeants First Class should seek generating force and broadening assignments, which could help separate them from their peers. Generating force and broadening assignments include Drill Sergeant, Recruiter, SLC Small Group Leader, Instructor, Training with Industry (TWI), HRC Enlisted Assignments NCO/ Professional Development NCO (PDNCO), Research Development Test & Evaluation (RDTE), and Special Agencies.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The best-qualified SFC will have 24 months of rated time in an authorized leadership position, or 12 months of rated time as a senior space operations sergeant or first sergeant. Possess one or more of the following qualifications: a consistently strong pattern of far exceeded standard ratings on their DA Forms 2166-9-2 with a consistent pattern of senior rater comments that clearly state strong potential to serve at the next higher grade, completion of 90 semester hours toward an associate degree or higher, or recognition as a Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate or top 20% Commandant’s list during NCOES or MOS enhancing course.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Reclassification
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: If an NCO at this grade reclassifies into Space Operations, they must complete CLD assignments within their new MOS before being considered for assignments in broadening opportunities.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Operational assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: At this point in their careers, SFC should be in operational assignments as a Platoon Sergeant, Section Leader, Operations Sergeant, or Systems/Master Evaluator. Boards and Leaders will view a minimum of 18 months to as qualified, 24 months as highly qualified, and 36 months or more as most qualified. SFCs should seek out assignments that complement their development as SNCO leaders, e.g., Career Management NCO, Writer/Instructor. Additionally, to compete for promotion to MSG requires successful service as a Platoon Sergeant, Section Leader, Operations Sergeant, or Systems/Master Evaluator. NCOs must document, on the DA Form 2166-9-2 (NCOER), their successful service in leadership positions at the next higher grade to be considered above their peers.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Education
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Advanced Leader Course (ALC) and Senior Leader Course (SLC).

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Key Developmental Assignments (KDAs)
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Platoon Sergeant, Section Leader, Operations Sergeant, or Systems/Master Evaluator.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Developmental/Broadening
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Senior Drill Sergeant, Inspector General NCO, Professional Development NCO-HRC, Senior Instructor/Writer, SLC Small Group Leader, Military Equal Opportunity Advisor (MEO Advisor), TWI, SARC/VA.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Self-Development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Airborne, Jumpmaster, Air Assault, Ranger, Master Fitness Trainer, Battle Staff, Master Driver Trainer, Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention (SHARP), Equal Opportunity Leader, HAZMAT Course, and Enlisted Aide Training Course.

passages.heading: Master Space Operations Sergeant (SFC) Development — Core Competencies
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Tactical and technical proficiency, Leadership, Planning and Executing Space Operations, Quality Assurance and Quality Control of staff level Space Products, Proficiency in Space Operations Fundamentals.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Master Sergeants/First Sergeants should focus on coaching and mentoring a battery/company and remain committed to excellence in their organizations by developing subordinates to be proficient in their duties. Limited assignment authorizations and competitive promotion to the SGM level dictate that Master Sergeants maintain the highest proficiency levels through the operational, institutional, and self-development domains. The Master Sergeant’s career progression relies upon a strong drive to excel in duty performance and space operations proficiency, in addition to the attainment of KSBs) related to leadership and MOS competency.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Master Sergeant/First Sergeant should study and master the following military publications: AR 220–1, AR 220-45, AR 600-8-2, AR 600–20, AR 601–280, AR 623-3, AR 840–10, DA Pam 611–21, and DA Pam 623-3.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Master sergeants should also continue to leverage other distributed learning programs and broaden their focus to include functional training. These NCOs must recognize their new role at the strategic level and pursue functional courses from various sources to enhance their understanding of how the Army operates, influence and improve its systems, and contribute to the success of their organizations.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Master Sergeants and First Sergeants should enroll in the Enlisted Joint Professional Military Education Course (EJPME) I and/or II and complete it within the allotted time through the JKO website. The Army expects a Master Sergeant/First Sergeant to serve as a key member of senior- level staff and take on senior leadership roles. Success in these positions requires proficiency in communication, operational expertise, and strong management skills.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Master Sergeants/First Sergeants should seek placement in generating and broadening assignments that will help them stand out among their peers. Generating and broadening assignments, e.g., TWI, HRC Enlisted Assignments NCO, Professional Development NCO (PDNCO), Senior Career Manager, and Senior Instructor.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The best-qualified MSG will have 24 months of rated time in an authorized leadership position, or 24 months of rated time as a senior space operations sergeant or first sergeant. Possess one or more of the following qualifications: a consistently strong pattern of far exceeded standard ratings on their DA Forms 2166-9-2 with a consistent pattern of senior rater comments that clearly state strong potential to serve at the next higher grade, completion of a degree program (Bachelor’s or Master’s degree) or accumulate 120 semester hours of college credit towards a degree, or recognition as a Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate or top 20% Commandant’s list during NCOES or MOS enhancing courses.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Operational assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The key developmental assignment for MSGs is the First Sergeant position. This position qualifies MSGs to perform duties as the Senior NCO of a unit and enhances their organizational supervisory knowledge, leadership skills, and abilities. MSGs should serve successfully as a First Sergeant for a minimum of 18 months. When not assigned as a unit 1SG, the MSG should seek opportunities to serve in developmental positions, such as Operations Sergeant or SEA/SEL. Successful performance in these positions is a conditional prerequisite for consideration to SGM.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Education
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Senior Leader Course (SLC) and Master Leader Course (MLC).

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Key Developmental Assignments (KDAs)
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: NCOPDS School Chief, US Military Training Mission (USMTM) NCO, GMD NCO, Senior Observer/Controller Trainer, Combat Division Staff NCO (CDID), DOTD Operations NCOIC, and AC/RC Chief Advisor, Battle Staff NCO.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Developmental/Broadening
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: CMF proponent, Senior Military Science Instructor, Common Faculty Development -Instructor Course (CFD-IC), Chief Instructor of an Army Service School.

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Self-Development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Complete a bachelor’s degree if not already completed or higher- level civilian education. Attend CMF-related courses on leadership, team building, organizational management, and problem-solving techniques. Attend Enlisted Joint Professional Military Education (EPJME) Phase I course. Airborne, Air Assault, Jumpmaster, BSNCOC, Senior Enlisted Joint Professional Military Education (SEJPME) Course II, Mission Command Digital Master Gunner Course, Capabilities Development Course, Operational Contract Support Course (OCS), SHARP Foundations Course, Master Fitness Trainer, and Company Commander & First Sergeant Pre- Command Course (CCFSPCC).

passages.heading: xi. Space Operations Senior NCO (MSG) Development — Core Competencies
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Tactical and technical proficiency, Leadership, Mastery of Troop Leading Procedures, Proficiency in the Military Decision-Making Process, Mastery of Space Operations Fundamentals.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The Sergeant Major/Command Sergeant Major is the subject matter expert and senior enlisted leader for the Space Operations organization. Senior NCOs at this level should be proficient in organizational leadership and develop skills that enhance strategic leadership through professional development at the battalion/brigade/division levels. The academic goals of the Sergeants Major/Command Sergeants Major should center on completion of a bachelor’s degree and efforts toward a Master’s degree in their chosen discipline. Activities such as professional reading or college courses help the Senior NCO develop the organizational leadership skills needed to coach, teach, and mentor Soldiers. The sheer number of Soldiers whose influence and interactions a Senior NCO’s reach encompasses demands outstanding communication skills. Skills in community and public relations are also crucial, as the Sergeant Major/Command Sergeants Major will often represent the command or the Army at various civic functions. The Sergeants Major/Command Sergeants Major should be the foremost enlisted expert on professional writing and communication skills within their formations and should develop subordinates’ professional communication abilities.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — The SGMs and CSMs should take advantage of TC 7–22
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: 7, which contains more reading material for self-development. Continued professional reading on world politics, geopolitical issues, and field manuals related to Army operations and current battle doctrine expands a leader’s knowledge.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: SGM/CSMs should assess the organization to help guide it towards the Commander’s organizational goals and desired end-state. SGM/CSMs link staff with subordinate echelons, while ensuring the proliferation of the Commander’s Intent at all levels. SGM/CSMs build competence throughout the formation by leveraging institutional domains and training opportunities.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Operational assignments
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: The principal assignment for SGMs, other than CSM, is a battalion-level or higher operations sergeant or staff assignment at the division level or above.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Education
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Master Leaders Course (MLC) and selection to the Sergeants Major Academy.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Key Developmental Assignments (KDAs)
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Battalion-level or higher operations sergeant or staff assignment at the Division level or above.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Developmental/Broadening
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: SMC Instructor, Proponent SGM, Enlisted Branch SGM, NCOLCoE Instructor, NCOLCoE Fellowship assignments, Assistant Inspector General (IG), Congressional Fellowship.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Self-Development
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body: Enlisted Joint Professional Military Education Course II (EJPME II), How the Army Runs (HTAR); Nominative Leaders Course (NLC); Keystone Course Force Management Course; Battalion/Brigade Pre-Command Course (BBPCC), Manpower/Force Development.

passages.heading: xii. Space Operations Senior NCO (SGM/CSM) Development — Core Competencies
passages.chapter: Chapter 40-7. Space Operations Specialist (MOS 40D) Essential Capabilities and development
passages.body:
Tactical and technical proficiency, Expert in Leadership, Mastery of Troop Leading Procedures, Mastery of the Military Decision-Making Process, Mastery in Space Operations Fundamentals.
10. Active Guard Reserve (AGR), Reserve Component (USAR), National Guard (ARNG) Space Operations Specialist Life Cycle.
i. Active Guard Reserve. Talent Management Division (TMD) at HRC, ICW, the AGR Career Manager, provides guidance regarding assignments, schools, and promotions of AGR Soldiers. ii. Reserve Component. Career Management Officers (CMOs) and Army Reserve Career Counselors (ARCCs) ICW the Soldier’s Chain of command, review Soldier career paths and control future assignments. iii. National Guard. ARNG at the state level conducts career management boards and controls ARNG Soldier assignments. RC and ARNG Soldiers are encouraged to be aware of the Active Component Space Operations Specialist Career cycle. iv. Specialist to Sergeant Major Development. RC/ARNG and Active-Duty Space Operations Specialists Career Life Cycles follow a similar career timeline.
